name: Learn several yo-yo tricks
blurb: A modern responsive yo-yo makes the first five tricks reachable in a fortnight: sleeper, walk the dog, around the world, rock the baby and the trapeze.
gear: A responsive ball-bearing yo-yo (not a cheap fixed-axle toy)
Spare strings — they wear out fast
steps: Set the string length: standing with the yo-yo on the floor, the string should reach your navel. Tie the loop for your middle finger correctly.
Master the sleeper — a smooth throw straight down that spins in place for several seconds — before anything else. Every trick depends on it.
Learn the return: a slight tug at the bottom of the sleeper brings it back to the hand.
Learn walk the dog and around the world, both of which are just a sleeper plus one movement.
Learn rock the baby, which teaches you to make string figures with a spinning yo-yo.
Learn the trapeze — landing the yo-yo on the string — which opens the door to the whole string-trick family.
tips: A yo-yo that dies after two seconds means a crooked throw, not a bad yo-yo. Throw straight down the plane of your arm.
Wind it neatly. A badly wound string wrecks the next throw.
Replace the string when it looks fuzzy, roughly every few hours of play.
proof: You perform five distinct tricks in a row, each landing cleanly, on demand.
